sections.h2: What makes the Melissa market different from other Collin County cities?
sections.html:
Melissa is small, young and almost entirely owner-occupied, so most competing listings are recent construction. An older or unrenovated house has to stand beside builder product with current finishes.

The Census Bureau counted 4,695 residents in 2010 and 13,901 in 2020, then estimated 29,969 on July 1, 2025. That is 115.6 percent above the 2020 base, among the fastest growth in the state. Children make up 30.7 percent of residents, and only 6.7 percent are 65 or older.

  • Working with an agent suits a house in good order and a seller with weeks to wait.
  • Selling on your own fits an owner at ease with contracts and disclosures.
  • Cash suits a house that needs work, has a tenant or faces a deadline.

sections.h2: What do the numbers show about Melissa homes and incomes?
sections.html:
Melissa is an owner-heavy, high-income city. For 2020-2024 the owner-occupied rate was 88.7 percent, the median home value $454,000 and the median household income $138,763.

The 33.6 minute commute is the longest of the four cities in this group, so many residents drive to jobs elsewhere in the Dallas area. Households average 3.26 people, the largest figure here, and 52.6 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Poverty sits at 1.9 percent.

Melissa is on U.S. Highway 75 about seven miles northeast of McKinney in north central Collin County. Settlers arrived in the 1840s for the Blackland Prairie soil, and the town was laid out in 1872 when the Houston and Texas Central Railway came through.

The Handbook of Texas says a post office opened in May 1873 and an electric interurban line tied the town to Dallas from 1908. A tornado on April 13, 1921 killed thirteen people, and a fire later burned many rebuilt buildings. The population slid to 285 by 1949.

Incorporation came in the early 1970s, with 604 residents in 1980 and 1,350 in 2000. Nearly everything people buy and sell in Melissa went up after that, which is why most houses are only a few years old.

sections.h2: Which Collin County offices matter when selling in Melissa?
sections.html:
Collin County offices handle Melissa houses. Values and exemption filings go to the Collin Central Appraisal District, while the county clerk files the deed.

  • Open your account on the district's property search and check that the homestead exemption is in place.
  • The district's homepage said 2026 notices of appraised value for real property would go out April 15.
  • A protest of value goes to the Collin appraisal review board.
  • New subdivisions may carry special district charges, so ask what appears on your bill.

Get the payoff figure from the county tax office ahead of closing.

sections.h2: What local building rules should a Melissa seller know?
sections.html:
Melissa's rules on extra dwellings are worth checking if your lot has a casita, garage apartment or similar structure. A city page written about a 2025 state bill said Melissa allowed accessory dwelling units only in its larger single-family zones, on lots over 10,000 square feet, with review of parking, spacing and setbacks.

State law can change what a city allows, so treat that page as background and ask the city's planning staff what applies to your lot today. The same city page noted a separate state law that bars cities from regulating exterior construction products that a national building code allows.

  • Ask the city whether any added structure on the lot was permitted.
  • Collect permits and final inspections for any addition, because lenders and inspectors ask for them.
  • Check your HOA documents, because most newer Melissa subdivisions have them.

Work done without a permit is a classic cause of a delayed closing. Sorting it out before you list keeps the timeline in your hands.

sections.h2: How do Texas property tax dates affect a newer Melissa home?
sections.html:
The tax lien for a year attaches on January 1, which is also the date the appraisal district uses to value the house. A mid-year closing therefore deals with a bill that is already building.

  • The statewide school homestead exemption is $140,000, and an owner who is 65 or older or disabled adds $60,000.
  • Someone buying after January 1 may claim the exemption for the remainder of that year when the seller never had one.
  • Homestead valuation notices arrive about April 1, and exemption filings must come in before May 1.

With higher values, tax can be a meaningful line on the closing statement, so have the title company show the proration before you sign.

sections.h2: What if a Melissa house has a tenant, heir or default?
sections.html:
Rentals are scarce, with a median gross rent of $2,532, so most buyers plan to live in the house. If a tenant is in place, written notice to vacate is generally three days unless the lease differs, and the tenant is sued in justice court if they stay. Set the closing date with the lease end in mind.

After an owner's death, heirs have four years to probate a will, or they can file a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship with the county clerk. A servicer's notice of sale comes at least 21 days before the auction.

sections.h2: What do Melissa buyers look for?
sections.html:
Buyers here tend to be families with children, and the Census Bureau shows 7.1 percent of residents under five and 30.7 percent under 18. They commute: the mean trip is 33.6 minutes, so access to U.S. Highway 75 and travel time to McKinney and Dallas come up often.

Connectivity matters too. The Census Bureau lists 99.0 percent of households with a computer and 98.1 percent with broadband, which suits remote workers. Retail sales were $463,846 thousand in 2022, so most shopping happens close by, and the city has 884 veterans among its residents.

  • Show recent upgrades, because competing listings are nearly new.
  • Gather HOA documents and any warranty paperwork early.
  • Be ready for a buyer whose own house must sell first, which can lengthen a closing.

Of residents, 17.3 percent were born abroad and 23.9 percent of those age five and up speak another language at home, so flexible communication with buyers helps.

Melissa packs growth into a small footprint. The city covers 11.45 square miles, up from 10.11 in 2010, and population density rose from 464.3 people per square mile in 2010 to 1,213.8 in 2020, based on Census figures.

Only 81.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, a lower share than in Mansfield or McKinney, which reflects the steady arrival of new owners. For a seller, that churn means active buyer traffic, but it also means your neighbors may have moved in recently and your street may be only a few years old. Newer subdivisions bring uniform lots, so condition, upgrades and the location of your lot within the neighborhood tend to set the price spread.

faqs.q: Which county is Melissa, TX in?
faqs.a: Collin County, in its north central part near McKinney. The Collin Central Appraisal District and county clerk handle your values and deed.
Very fast. The Census Bureau counted 13,901 residents in 2020 and estimated 29,969 for July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Melissa house with a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes, though many buyers want to move in. Check the lease end date and give written notice if you need the tenant out.

faqs.q: What exemption applies to a Melissa homestead?
faqs.a: The base is $140,000 from the school district, with $60,000 added at age 65 or on disability. Apply to the appraisal district by the end of April.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell my late parent's Melissa house?
faqs.a: Usually some court or recorded step comes first. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death skips probate.
